articles.title: Americanas tem prejuízo de R$ 352 milhões no 3º trimestre | G1
articles.standfirst: No mesmo período do ano passado, a varejista havia registrado lucro de R$ 367 milhões.
articles.summary: No mesmo período do ano passado, a varejista havia registrado lucro de R$ 367 milhões.
articles.body:
Clientes fizeram fila na frente das Lojas Americanas, no Salvador Shopping — Foto: Divulgação

A rede varejista Americanas, que saiu da recuperação judicial em outubro, registrou prejuízo líquido de R$ 352 milhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026 , segundo balanço divulgado nesta quarta-feira (11). No mesmo período do ano passado, a companhia havia registrado lucro de R$ 367 milhões.

O resultado operacional medido pelo lucro antes de juros, impostos, depreciação e amortização (Ebitda) ajustado caiu de R$ 558 milhões para R$ 52 milhões na comparação anual.

Apesar do prejuízo, a receita líquida da companhia cresceu 10% no trimestre, para R$ 2,97 bilhões. As vendas nas mesmas lojas, indicador que considera unidades em funcionamento há pelo menos um ano, avançaram 7,3%.

No acumulado de janeiro a setembro, a Americanas atribuiu a piora do resultado principalmente à ausência de ganhos extraordinários que haviam beneficiado o balanço de 2025, especialmente de natureza tributária, tanto no resultado operacional quanto no financeiro.

Relembre o escândalo contábil na Americanas

O escândalo da Americanas veio à tona em 11 de janeiro de 2023, quando as Americanas divulgaram um fato relevante informando que haviam sido identificadas "inconsistências em lançamentos contábeis" nos balanços corporativos, estimadas inicialmente em cerca de R$ 20 bilhões.

Segundo a companhia, os valores referentes aos primeiros nove meses de 2022 e a exercícios anteriores não haviam sido registrados de forma adequada.

À época, o então presidente Sergio Rial deixou o cargo apenas nove dias após assumir a função, assim como o diretor financeiro André Covre.

Na ocasião, a empresa informou que havia detectado operações de financiamento de compras em valores da mesma ordem de grandeza, nas quais era devedora perante instituições financeiras, mas que não estavam adequadamente refletidas nas demonstrações financeiras.

No dia seguinte, 12 de janeiro, a revelação provocou forte turbulência no mercado financeiro . Instituições financeiras colocaram as ações das Americanas sob revisão, enquanto a B3 chegou a submeter os papéis da companhia a leilão diante da volatilidade.

Ao final do pregão, as ações acumulavam queda de 77,33%, uma das maiores perdas diárias já registradas por uma empresa de capital aberto no Brasil.

Naquele momento, Sergio Rial afirmou que o problema não se referia a valores inexistentes, mas sim a registros contábeis feitos de forma inadequada ao longo dos anos. Ele também explicou que a origem das inconsistências estava nas operações de risco sacado.

🔎 O risco sacado é uma modalidade comum no varejo em que uma instituição financeira antecipa o pagamento devido a fornecedores e passa a ser credora da empresa. No caso das Americanas essas obrigações não apareciam corretamente nos balanços, o que fazia reduzir artificialmente o endividamento da companhia.

As investigações também apontam irregularidades envolvendo verbas de propaganda cooperada (VPCs), incentivos comerciais concedidos por fornecedores ao varejo.

Em 13 de janeiro de 2023, a Justiça do Rio de Janeiro concedeu uma medida cautelar protegendo as Americanas contra o vencimento antecipado de dívidas , suspendendo temporariamente cobranças enquanto a empresa avaliava um eventual pedido de recuperação judicial.

A decisão buscava impedir que credores esgotassem rapidamente os ativos da companhia e preservasse sua atividade econômica.

Na mesma época, também vieram à tona informações de que executivos haviam vendido aproximadamente R$ 212 milhões em ações da empresa durante o segundo semestre de 2022, levantando suspeitas de uso de informação privilegiada.

O pedido de recuperação judicial veio apenas oito dias após a revelação das inconsistências contábeis , em 19 de janeiro de 2023. Na ocasião, a companhia informou possuir apenas R$ 800 milhões em caixa, valor muito inferior aos R$ 8,6 bilhões divulgados no balanço do terceiro trimestre de 2022, tornando sua situação financeira insustentável.

Posteriormente, a recuperação judicial tornou-se uma das maiores da história empresarial brasileira, envolvendo dívidas superiores a R$ 50 bilhões.

Em março de 2026, a companhia informou que havia cumprido as obrigações previstas no plano de recuperação judicial com vencimento até dois anos após sua homologação e protocolou o pedido de encerramento do processo . A Justiça aceitou o encerramento, marcando a saída formal da empresa da recuperação judicial.

*Com informações da agência de notícias Reuters.

articles.title: Brick houses are disappearing from America’s new construction: ‘Nobody got paid for how long a house would last’
articles.summary: Brick or brick veneer now covers just 16.8% of new homes. Real structural brick walls are rarer still, as builders trade permanence for speed.
articles.body:
Americans have never paid more for a home. The median existing home sold for a record $440,600 in June , according to the National Association of Realtors. Yet the brick house, the kind built to stand for a century, has nearly vanished from new construction.

Brick or brick veneer covered just 16.8% of new single-family homes started in 2025, down from almost a quarter in 2012, according to a National Association of Home Builders analysis of Census data . And most of the homes that still look like brick houses aren't. They're wood-frame houses with a layer of brick veneer attached to the outside.

A home can mean a lot of things. A place to raise a family. An investment. A refuge. A milestone . But somewhere along the way, American homebuilding changed the question. Not "will this last a lifetime?" Just "will it last the mortgage?"

"We didn't decide to build houses that just outlast the mortgage. We kind of drifted there," said Dan D'Agostino, founder of Plan Architecture and a residential architect based in New Jersey.

The distinction between real brick and veneer matters. A structural masonry wall holds up the building itself. Veneer is an exterior finish, while the wood frame behind it does the structural work.

The change reflects a postwar housing boom, a shrinking skilled-labor pool, rising construction costs, and a preference for homes that could be built quickly and cheaply. But some architects and builders say it also changed what Americans expect from the places they live, and what buyers paying record prices actually get for their money.

Why builders traded masonry for wood framing

The shift away from structural masonry accelerated after World War II, when returning veterans and their families needed affordable homes, and needed them quickly. Developers such as Levitt & Sons met that demand with standardized designs and faster construction methods. Between 1947 and 1951, the company built 17,447 houses in Levittown on Long Island , at times finishing 10 to 12 homes a day.

"Levittown was a legitimate solution to a genuine crisis," Steven Menotti, CEO of construction safety company Menotti Enterprise, told Fortune . "They needed shelter urgently, and a carpentry team got the job done faster than a masonry team ever would have."

Brick construction requires skilled workers to lay individual bricks, one at a time. Wood framing can be assembled by crews with less specialized training, and it moves much faster. Matt DiBara, CEO of DiBara Masonry and a fourth-generation stonemason, said the economics were simple.

articles.title: Long US Bonds Reopen With Gains as Risk Sentiment Sours Again
articles.summary: Long-end Treasuries drifted higher as trading resumed after a holiday as turmoil at Nvidia Corp. fueled doubts about the artificial intelligence trade and fu...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Long-end Treasuries drifted higher as trading resumed after a holiday as turmoil at Nvidia Corp. fueled doubts about the artificial intelligence trade and fueled demand for haven assets.

Yields on 30-year US government bonds slipped two basis points to 5.34% ahead of an auction of similar-maturity securities on Thursday. Those on 10-year notes dipped briefly before steadying at 4.99%. There was no cash trading on Wednesday due to the Veterans' Day holiday.

Risk sentiment took a hit after a report said Nvidia's board was considering the removal of Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang following allegations of multiple extramarital affairs. The chipmaker sits at the heart of the AI trade, meaning any sign of trouble risks undermining confidence far beyond the firm itself.

"All these headlines on Jensen Huang are further sowing doubt about the AI story and triggering a small safe haven bid in Treasuries," said Carol Kong, strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia. "There is no doubt every market participant is watching this closely given how critical Nvidia is to the AI investment boom, and by extension, the global economy."

Other government bonds were also in demand in Asia trading, with yields on Australian and New Zealand debt slipping at least one basis point.

Nasdaq futures dropped almost 1% and S&P contracts declined 0.5% after Nvidia tumbled about 10% in late trading. The company's board is meeting to discuss Huang's future after he admitted to an affair with a woman US officials reportedly believe is a Chinese spy, according to a person familiar with the matter.

"Aggressive traders will likely view any modest Nasdaq bounce as a window to re-set macro hedges. It may also revitalize the bid for bonds, which have been struggling this week."

Mark Cranfield, strategist at Markets Live

But shorter-end Treasuries edged lower as traders held fast to bets for more Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes, leading to a flattening of the curve. Yields on two-year notes climbed three basis points to 4.77% and those on five-year debt rose one basis point to 4.83%.

The swaps market indicates that traders are pricing in a quarter-point rate increase at the Fed's December meeting after a key gauge of US consumer prices posted another firm advance in October. The print prompted Fed officials to open the door to more aggressive rate increases over the coming months, with Governor Christopher Waller saying a half-percentage-point hike in December may be needed.

articles.title: Nvidia has lost $450 billion since Jensen Huang admitted to an affair. Millions of 401(k)s are exposed
articles.summary: Two retirement experts explain how much of a typical 401(k) rides on Nvidia and why savers should sit tight.
articles.body:
Nvidia shares fell nearly 8% in after-hours trading Wednesday after the Wall Street Journal reported that the chipmaker's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang . The board could meet imminently to decide his future, the report said.

The stock had closed the regular session up about 3%, at $173.73, before sliding to roughly $160 in post-market trading, per Yahoo Finance . The same day, The New York Times reported that Huang had a second extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care.

The turmoil began Nov. 8, when Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International whom U.S. officials believe is an agent of China's Ministry of State Security, per the AP . The two are not related. Nvidia has since lost more than $450 billion in market value, according to CBS News .

That selloff reaches well past Wall Street. Nvidia, No. 16 on the 2026 Fortune 500, was worth about $4.1 trillion at Wednesday's close, second only to Apple, according to Companies Market Cap . A company that size sits inside the index funds and target-date funds that anchor millions of Americans' 401(k)s, whether those savers chose it or not.

Founded in April 1993 and public since January 1999, Nvidia became the first company ever to reach a $5.5 trillion market cap in May 2026, per Yahoo Finance . Several experts Fortune spoke with said that while the details of Alice Huang's background and affiliations remain murky, the implications for the average investor are already fairly clear.

"The average American's exposure to NVIDIA stock volatility depends on how they invest, but a reasonable estimate is 3% to 5%," Leonard Gilroy , senior managing director of the Reason Foundation's Pension Integrity Project, told Fortune .

"NVIDIA represents about 6% of the total market capitalization of the S&P 500 and about 10% of the total market cap of the NASDAQ100," he said. "If an individual had 100% of their retirement invested in an S&P 500 or NASDAQ100 index fund and NVIDIA hypothetically lost 100% of its value, they could see a direct investment loss of about 5% to 10%."

That would be the worst case, and most retirement accounts are spread far more broadly. "About 70% of 401(k)s are invested in public equities," Gilroy said, "and many investors hold a mix of index funds and target-date funds, which reduces exposure to one company."

Public pensions are even less exposed. The Reason Foundation estimates that Nvidia accounts for about 2.5% of the average public pension fund's assets, Gilroy said, "since they are typically more diversified, with public equities accounting for only 46% of assets under management."

articles.title: India back among world’s top 5 biggest stock markets with record rally; value climbs to $5.4 trillion
articles.summary: India has reclaimed its position as the world’s fifth largest stock market by value, courtesy the record rally its indices have seen in the last ten
articles.body: India has reclaimed its position as the world’s fifth largest stock market by value, courtesy the record rally its indices have seen in the last ten trading sessions.Indian equities have gained around $640 billion in market value since late October, benefiting from weakening investor enthusiasm for AI-related stocks and a steep fall in oil prices.Bank of America has raised its estimate for India’s economic growth in the third quarter of 2026 to 7.7% year-on-year, compared with its earlier projection of 7.2%, a report published earlier this week showed.Moody’s too has lifted the growth forecast from 6.5% to 7%. Global brokerages have upgraded their outlook for the stock market.Also Read | Sensex erases US-Iran war losses, rises nearly 12% in just 10 sessions: What should your investment strategy be?India back in top 5 leagueThe rally has lifted the market’s total value to approximately $5.4 trillion, allowing India to overtake Taiwan and reclaim its position as the world’s fifth-largest stock market, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.The shift in global investment flows has also set India apart from other markets. While overseas investors are returning to Indian equities, Taiwan recorded its highest-ever foreign fund outflows in October as AI-linked stocks came under a worldwide selloff.The developments prompted authorities there to introduce measures to support the market. articles.title: Binance Blockchain Week 2026 to bring global finance, crypto and policy leaders to Bangkok
articles.summary: Binance, the leading global financial platform powered by blockchain, has announced the first wave of speaker line-up for the Binance Blockchain Week
articles.body: Binance, the leading global financial platform powered by blockchain, has announced the first wave of speaker line-up for the Binance Blockchain Week (BBW) Bangkok 2026. The flagship event returns to Asia on November 28-29, 2026, at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center, marking a strategic homecoming as traditional finance and digital assets converge across the region's rapidly expanding markets.Under this year's theme, Evolve, the program reflects an inflection point in digital finance: traditional and digital markets are converging on shared infrastructure, AI is reshaping how people access information and manage capital, and governments, institutions and builders are increasingly collaborating on the clear, trusted frameworks for sustainable industry growth. Payments, tokenized stocks, real-world assets, and digital assets are merging into one connected system, while the barriers to entry for people around the world continue to fall.Binance Blockchain Week (BBW) Bangkok 2026 will bring leading pan-regional policymakers together, including Gizzat Baitursynov, Vice Minister, Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development of the Republic of Kazakhstan, and Shaun Tan, Head of Crypto and Fintech Growth, Gelephu Mindfulness City (GMC), Bhutan. Their presence reflects a defining shift, as regulators and builders increasingly work side by side to set clear guardrails.Speaking on the announcement, Richard Teng, Co-CEO of Binance, said, “Regulatory innovation is no longer confined to traditional financial centers. Increasingly, emerging jurisdictions are shaping the future of digital finance. The regulatory frameworks and financial infrastructure countries build today will determine where capital flows, where companies choose to grow, and which markets lead tomorrow. We're grateful to convene this critical dialogue in Bangkok."The program brings together recognised leaders across finance, technology, and digital assets, including Arthur Hayes, CIO of Maelstrom, who invented the perpetual swap now one of the most widely traded products in crypto; Sushant Singh, APAC Expansion, Tether; Matthew Roszak, Chairman, Bloq; and CZ (Changpeng Zhao), founder, Giggle Academy and Binance.As traditional finance and digital assets converge, the lineup follows the money on-chain. Leaders from global financial institutions, payments networks, and technology companies will join them, including Dan Maley, APAC Head of Digital Assets, BlackRock; Roger Bayston, Head of Digital Assets Ecosystem Development, Franklin Templeton; Kelly Sohn, Head of Digital Asset, Mirae Asset Securities (HK) Limited; Min Linn, Managing Director, Head of Global Business Development, Ondo Finance; Nischint Sanghavi, Head of Digital Currencies, Asia Pacific, Visa; Athena Y, CEO, United Stables; Yuki Jinguji, Head of Financial Business Development, PayPay Corporation; Thomas Chen, Chief Business Officer, BNB Chain; Yoshi Yokokawa, Co-Founder and CEO, Alpaca; and Ella Zhang, Managing Partner & Head of YZi Labs.The program will also feature leading voices in crypto media, research, and on-chain data, including Nic Puckrin, Founder, Coin Bureau; Joshua de Vos, Research lead, CoinDesk; Alex Svanevik, CEO, Nansen; Anastasia Melachrinos, Head of Research, Kaiko; and Roosa Kivisto, Head of Business Development, DeFiLlama."As traditional finance and digital assets converge, our focus remains constant: improving access, strengthening user protections, and delivering seamless experiences," said Yi He, Co-CEO and Co-Founder of Binance. "Under this year's theme, Evolve, Binance Blockchain Week convenes the architects of this transformation," Yi added.The stage will also feature key leaders from Binance: Richard Teng, Co-CEO; Yi He, Co-CEO and Co-Founder; Eowyn Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; SB Seker, Head of APAC; Catherine Chen, Head of VIP and Institutional; Shunyet Jan, Head of Exchange and Trading; Thomas Gregory, VP of Payments and Fiat; Jeff Li, VP of Product; Antonio Alvarez Lorenzo, Deputy Chief Compliance Officer; and Nirun Fuwattananukul, CEO of Binance TH by Gulf Binance. More speakers will be announced in the coming weeks.The Road to Binance Blockchain Week on Binance LiveThe conversation starts before Bangkok with a special pre-event Binance Live session on November 17 at 11:00 UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) on Binance Square, featuring exclusive guests and a $5,000 red packet giveaway. It's an early look at the themes shaping this year's event and a chance to be part of the build-up from anywhere.What to expect at BBWAfter electrifying editions in Singapore, Istanbul, Paris, and Dubai, Binance group's flagship event returns to Asia at a pivotal moment: as traditional finance and crypto rails increasingly merge, Bangkok emerges as ground zero for the infrastructure connecting the two. Over two days, thousands of builders, institutional investors, fintech leaders, and policymakers will gather to define what comes next for digital assets.Binance Blockchain Week is the brand’s flagship gathering, representing the pinnacle of its 1,500 global events, where the brightest minds in blockchain come together to shape the future of digital finance. From high-level government dialogues to grassroots community engagement, the event bridges all corners of the ecosystem. articles.title: RBI plans to ban private equity firms from holding controlling stakes in multiple NBFCs: What will change?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is considering banning private equity firms from holding controlling stakes in more than one non-banking
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is considering banning private equity firms from holding controlling stakes in more than one non-banking financial company (NBFC).The proposed rules will also distinguish between controlling stakes and smaller financial investments, allowing holdings of 15% or less to attract fewer regulatory checks, sources told Reuters.The move follows the central bank's concerns that financial stress at a global private equity firm or its affiliates could spread across several NBFCs in which it has significant investments.However, the RBI also wants to encourage smaller financial investments that would be subject to less scrutiny, the people said, requesting anonymity as the discussions are private.What is controlling stakeCurrently, a 25% stake in a listed company is considered a controlling stake. However, an investor can also be considered to have control with a smaller shareholding if it can appoint most of the company's directors or influence its management or policy decisions.Investments of 15% or less will be treated as financial investments and face fewer regulatory checks, one of the people said.The RBI will finalise a draft of the proposed rules after seeking public feedback. The rules could be formally issued early next year, the person added.Foreign investors step up investments in NBFCsForeign investors have been showing growing interest in Indian banks and NBFCs, supported by strong demand for credit and low loan delinquencies.Private equity investments in India's financial sector reached around $5.4 billion last year, up 6% from 2024 and 17% from 2023, according to Grant Thornton data. A further $3.6 billion flowed into the sector between January and the end of September this year.The RBI has previously taken steps to prevent investors from holding controlling stakes in multiple NBFCs.Last year, the central bank approved US private equity firm Bain Capital's acquisition of a 41.7% stake in Manappuram Finance on the condition that it sell its 93% holding in another NBFC, Tyger Capital, formerly known as Adani Capital.The same approach has also applied to investors outside the private equity industry.Japan's Mizuho Financial Group holds majority stakes in two NBFCs, Mizuho Capsave and Credit Saison India. It has also announced plans to acquire KKR-backed financial services firm Avendus.The apex bank has asked Mizuho to submit a detailed plan to integrate or consolidate its existing non-bank financial businesses in India. Mizuho Securities did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.Industry seeks greater flexibility in ownership rulesThe Indian Venture and Alternate Capital Association has approached the RBI, seeking permission for different entities within the same group to hold stakes of more than 20% in multiple NBFCs.Siddarth M Pai, co-chair of the association's regulatory affairs committee and founder of venture capital firm 3one4 Capital, said many private equity firms and venture capital funds wanted to invest in fintech and financial services businesses through their different funds. However, ownership limits were making it difficult for them to do so.The sector has also seen two major private equity deals this week. Blackstone agreed to buy a 16% stake in IIFL Finance for $535 million, while Singapore's Temasek will invest around $265 million in Godrej Capital.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Kia India giving a major boost to its Andhra Pradesh manufacturing operations, with a $2 billion investment in a new plant.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Kia India giving a major boost to its Andhra Pradesh manufacturing operations, with a $2 billion investment in a new plant. The proposed facility is expected to create around 12,000 jobs and take the South Korean automaker's annual production capacity to 6.3 lakh vehicles.Kia India managing director and CEO Gwanggu Lee announced the expansion while speaking at the CII Partnership Summit on Thursday. "I am so delighted to announce the expansion of Kia's presence in Andhra Pradesh through the establishment of an additional manufacturing plant," he said.However, the company has not specified when it plans to make the investment or when the additional production capacity will become operational.Kia looks to ramp up production capacity to 6.3 lakhKia India currently has a manufacturing plant in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh, which was set up in 2017. The facility has an annual production capacity of 4.30 lakh vehicles. The proposed new plant will increase the company's total annual capacity to 6.30 lakh units.In financial year 2026, Kia India produced 3.17 lakh vehicles. Of these, 2.89 lakh units were dispatched in the domestic market, while 27,953 units were exported.Speaking about the company's growth in India, Lee said its first manufacturing plant in Andhra Pradesh was set up and commissioned in a record 14 months."Our journey in Andhra Pradesh began in 2017, when our first manufacturing plant was established and commissioned in a record time of just 14 months. Kia is proud of being among India's leading automotive manufacturers and the fastest OEM to achieve one million vehicle production in just four years and two million vehicles within seven years, Lee said.From electric to CNG: Kia plans launches across segmentsThe manufacturing expansion comes as Kia prepares to introduce several models across different powertrains to increase its share in India's passenger vehicle market.Apart from its battery-electric, petrol and diesel vehicles, the automaker is also planning to launch hybrid models. It has already announced its entry into the CNG segment with the Carens.Kia recently launched a facelifted version of its popular Seltos mid-size SUV and the new Sorento. The company expects both models to generate strong volumes going forward.The Korean giant's existing India portfolio also includes the Sonet, Syros, Carens and Carnival SUVs.Kia's manufacturing facility in Anantapur has also grown into an important export hub. The plant has exported more than 4.1 lakh vehicles and kits to nearly 100 countries.Lee said the facility's export operations have strengthened India's position as a global manufacturing powerhouse and supported the vision of Make it India for the world.You use AI every day. articles.title: India’s crude oil imports from Russia hit record high in October; Jamnagar refinery biggest importer
articles.summary: India's imports of Russian fossil fuels climbed to a record EUR 6.4 billion in October, fuelled by a steep rise in crude oil purchases, according to a
articles.body: India's imports of Russian fossil fuels climbed to a record EUR 6.4 billion in October, fuelled by a steep rise in crude oil purchases, according to a monthly analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).The increase has helped Russia record its highest monthly revenue from fossil fuel exports since December 2022, despite Western sanctions.China continued to lead the list of buyers worldwide. It accounted for 51% of Russia's export revenue from the five largest importing countries, with purchases worth EUR 10.7 billion.Also Read | Diversifying away from Russia: Trump admin wants to sell Venezuela oil to India, but how much can it buy?India’s record purchases from RussiaThe think tank noted that China and India, Russia's two biggest fossil fuel customers, both recorded their highest monthly purchases since January 2022. The figures underline Moscow's continued reliance on Asian markets, even as Western governments step up restrictions on its energy trade.China bought Russian fossil fuels worth EUR 10.7 billion during October, while India's purchases totalled EUR 6.4 billion. The European Union followed with imports worth EUR 2.2 billion. Turkiye ranked fourth, purchasing EUR 1.1 billion, while South Korea was fifth with imports of EUR 488 million."India was the second-largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels in October 2026, importing a total of EUR 6.4 billion of Russian hydrocarbons, its highest monthly total in data going back to January 2022. Crude oil constituted 91 per cent of India's purchases, totalling EUR 5.8 billion. Coal (EUR 333 million) and oil products (EUR 232 million) constituted the remainder of its monthly Russian imports," the report said."India's imports of Russian crude oil rose in October 2026, up 10% month-on-month. Russian crude imports rose at all three of India's largest importing refineries: (Nayara Energy's) Vadinar (up 12 per cent month-on-month), (Reliance Industries Ltd's) Jamnagar (up 22 per cent), and (Indian Oil Corporation Ltd's) Paradip (up 28 per cent)," CREA said."This increase has once again made the Jamnagar refinery the biggest importer of seaborne Russian crude."(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Countries imposing sanctions continue to importThe European Union ranked third among Russia's biggest fossil fuel buyers in October 2026. Its purchases accounted for 11 per cent of the export revenues generated by the top five importing countries, which was around EUR 2.2 billion.Refineries in India, Turkiye and Brunei processing Russian crude also shipped oil products worth EUR 1.6 billion to countries that had imposed sanctions on Russia following its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022."The destinations include the EU (EUR 1.2 billion), Australia (EUR 271 million), the US (EUR 94 million), and New Zealand (EUR 23 million). An estimated EUR 389 million of these products were refined from Russian crude."CREA said Russia's earnings from fossil fuel exports rose 14 per cent month-on-month in October to EUR 754 million a day, the highest monthly level since December 2022. Higher crude oil prices and record revenues from seaborne oil shipments helped counter the impact of Western sanctions, allowing Moscow to maintain its energy exports.Russia's export earnings increased even though its overall fossil fuel export volumes remained largely stable, indicating that higher international energy prices played a growing role in boosting its revenues. The rise also came amid elevated global oil and gas prices linked to the conflict in the Middle East and disruptions to energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.Exports travelling to the US in October came from India’s Jamnagar refinery (EUR 94 mn). Between August and October 2026, 30% of the Jamnagar refinery’s crude imports came from Russia.CREA estimated that the rise in oil and gas prices following the US-Israel strikes on Iran added $35.9 billion, or approximately EUR 31 billion, to Russia's seaborne fossil fuel export revenues over the following six months.You use AI every day.
